# An override names the target it implements by that target's identity const.
# A target's own package writes it unqualified, because the const is the
# package's own declaration -- `[android.platform]` inside android.sngl says
# the package's name twice. A program outside the package writes the qualified
# form, which is how the const reaches it at all.
#
# The bare name used to be refused before it was looked up: the index had to be
# a selector, so a target package could only name itself the long way.

sngl check qualified.sngl
stdout 'qualified.sngl: ok'

# The ambient `platform` type shares the name and is not an identity.
! sngl check bareuser.sngl
stderr 'not a target identity'

-- qualified.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:app"
import html "sngl:platform/html"

component mybox[html.platform] {
    text(value="html")
}

component mybox {
    text(value="generic")
}

window #home(title="t") {
    mybox
}
-- bareuser.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:app"
import html "sngl:platform/html"

component mybox[platform] {
    text(value="x")
}

component mybox {
    text(value="generic")
}

window #home(title="t") {
    mybox
}
